metadata.title: The Pressure-Supported Excess: What a Dark-Energy-Tied Galaxy Law Cannot Yet Explain, and Native-Input Shear Reruns on Both Footings (Working Note)
metadata.description:
Working note, version 1.0 (2026-10-21). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed.

Two more days of pre-registered tests (criteria frozen before computing, mutation controls, post-hoc amendments disclosed, both a0 footings 9.36e-11 and 1.13e-10 m/s^2 reported and never pooled) of a gravity framework with galactic law g_N = g^2/(g + a0), a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_DE), whose extra gravitating mass is a collisionless 'cold energy' component, not a particle.

(1) Shear: rerun at 1024^3 from the framework's own early-universe inputs, the framework's particle-mesh structure is CONSISTENT with raw KiDS-1000 cosmic shear against its matched Poisson control on both footings (Delta chi^2 -10.08 canonical, -9.39 alternative); on the alternative footing DES Y3 is diagnostic and also CONSISTENT (-2.15). The size of the lead is amplitude-driven (KiDS Delta chi^2 -3.11 to -15.80 canonical and -2.93 to -14.69 alternative over the projection Omega_m; about -2.9 / -2.8 with the framework's own covariance), neither arm is a good absolute fit, and the engine that produces the pass has no established physical parent (companion note PAPER57): the pass is a computational result of that engine. (2) CMB lensing: on raw Planck PR4 lensing (L 8-400) all four runs are indistinguishable from their controls, CONSISTENT only under a post-hoc amendment, with little power; a sealed Fisher forecast finds that S4-class lensing at L ~ 1000-2000 could separate them. (3) The pressure-supported excess: dwarfs, spheroidal lenses and cluster cores carry an excess over the law and rotating systems do not, but no single kinematic measure, local density or any of five candidate selectors sets the amounts, and the record's own cold-energy equations cannot select on kinematics. The cluster-core excess is not a baryon-census error and survives four small reframings. A stellar-IMF correction removes the red-lens excess if discs are not bottom-heavy; the dwarf excess survives every reframing tried; a fossil a0 helps only under the rival a0 proportional to H(z), which is reported as evidence about a0(z), not as a rescue.

Not derived: kappa = 1/2, the cold-to-baryon supply ratio, the retained fraction. A CONSISTENT class is not a preference. Companion notes: PAPER55 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23482936) and PAPER57. AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude (analysis lanes, review, drafting).
